prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1340; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a parking lot collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck while stationary. The claimant reports a wrist injury and is not represented by counsel.

Entry 2: Reviewed the driver's listing on the policy and confirmed the named driver is the person who was operating the vehicle at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report and witness statements. Both confirm the claimant was in the vehicle and that the impact occurred as described.

Entry 4: Photographs of the scene and the other driver's account match the reported sequence of events. Damage to the vehicle is consistent with the described impact, and no earlier damage is known.

Entry 5: Confirmed there is nothing indicating the damage predates the start of coverage. Policy effective dates were checked against the loss timeline.

Entry 6: Claimant has given the same account in every conversation so far. The reported wrist fracture is a plausible injury for a collision of this type.

Entry 7: Medical records show treatment ran somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. Claimant mentioned a minor strain to the same area years ago that healed fully; this will be noted for the medical review.
